examples.en: I am active as a labor union member at my company.

examples.ko: 노동조합원들이 오늘 임금 협상 결과를 투표로 정해요.
examples.en: The union members decide the wage negotiation result by vote today.

examples.ko: 우리 아버지는 오래된 노동조합원이라서 집회에 자주 가세요.
examples.en: My father is a longtime union member, so he often goes to rallies.
What do I have to do to become a union member?
Most union members took part in this strike.
We give this welfare benefit only to union members.

explain: 줄여서 '노조원'이라고도 많이 말해요. 파업, 임금 협상 같은 뉴스에 자주 나오는 말이에요. 노동조합에 들어 있는 사람을 말할 때는 '조합원'이라고만 해도 통해요.
explain_en: People often shorten it to '노조원'. It appears a lot in news about strikes and wage talks. In context, just '조합원' is also understood.

examples.en: The bread came out of the oven nicely golden brown.
Fry the pancake until both sides are golden.
The smell of golden-brown fried chicken is so good.
Wait until the outside turns golden brown.
I took out the sweet potatoes, roasted golden brown.
The cookies in the oven are already golden brown.

explain: 주로 빵, 전, 고기처럼 구운 음식이 먹음직스럽게 익은 색을 말할 때 써요. '누릇누릇하다'는 이것의 큰말이에요. 너무 익으면 '타다', '새까맣게 타다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is mostly used for the appetizing color of baked or fried food like bread, pancakes and meat. '누릇누릇하다' is its larger-sounding counterpart. If food cooks too long, you say '타다' (burn).

examples.ko: 상대 팀의 노림수가 뭔지 잘 모르겠어요.
examples.en: I don't know what the other team is aiming for.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 갑자기 친절해진 데에는 다른 노림수가 있는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think there's another motive behind his sudden kindness.

examples.ko: 이 광고의 노림수는 젊은 사람들의 관심을 끄는 거예요.
examples.en: The aim of this ad is to catch young people's attention.
The coach's strategy worked out exactly right.

examples.ko: 아무 노림수 없이 그냥 도와주고 싶었어요.
examples.en: I just wanted to help, with no hidden agenda.

examples.ko: 그 질문에는 분명히 노림수가 숨어 있어요.
examples.en: There is definitely a calculated aim hidden in that question.

explain: '속셈'은 숨겨 둔 생각이라는 느낌이 강하고, '노림수'는 결과를 얻으려고 짠 계산이나 전략에도 써요. 스포츠, 광고, 정치 이야기에 자주 나와요. '노림수가 있다', '노림수가 맞아떨어지다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: '속셈' feels like a hidden thought, while '노림수' can also mean a calculated move or strategy aimed at a result. It shows up often in sports, ads and politics. Common patterns are '노림수가 있다' and '노림수가 맞아떨어지다'.

examples.ko: 저는 노부모를 모시고 같이 살고 있어요.
examples.en: I live together with my elderly parents and take care of them.
I worry a lot about my elderly parents' hospital bills.

examples.ko: 형이 노부모를 돌보느라 휴가를 못 가요.
examples.en: My older brother can't take a vacation because he looks after our elderly parents.

examples.ko: 요즘은 노부모를 요양원에 모시는 가정도 있어요.
examples.en: These days some families place their elderly parents in a nursing home.
I call my elderly parents every week to check on them.
I have elderly parents, so it is hard to move far away.

explain: 글이나 뉴스에서 많이 쓰고, 보통 말할 때는 그냥 '부모님'이라고 해요. '노부모를 모시다', '노부모를 부양하다'가 자주 쓰는 짝이에요. 남의 부모님이든 내 부모님이든 쓸 수 있지만 직접 부를 때는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It is common in writing and news, while in everyday speech people just say '부모님'. Typical pairings are '노부모를 모시다' and '노부모를 부양하다'. You can use it for anyone's parents, but never to address them directly.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 노숙인을 위한 쉼터가 문을 열어요.
examples.en: In winter, shelters for homeless people open up.

examples.ko: 역 근처에서 노숙인에게 따뜻한 국을 나눠 줬어요.
examples.en: We handed out warm soup to homeless people near the station.

examples.ko: 지하철역에서 노숙인 한 분이 주무시고 계셨어요.
examples.en: A homeless person was sleeping in the subway station.
City Hall started a jobs program for homeless people.
The government supports housing so that homelessness decreases.
I volunteer at a soup kitchen for homeless people every weekend.

explain: '노숙자'라고도 하지만 뉴스나 공문서에서는 '노숙인'을 더 많이 써요. 사람을 낮춰 부르는 느낌을 줄이려고 쓰는 말이에요. 길에서 자는 일은 '노숙하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: '노숙자' is also used, but news and official documents prefer '노숙인', which sounds less demeaning. The act of sleeping outdoors is '노숙하다'.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 노인정에는 할머니들이 매일 모여요.
examples.en: Grandmothers gather every day at the senior center in our neighborhood.
My grandfather goes to the senior center after lunch.
The elders are playing yut at the senior center.

examples.ko: 아파트 단지 안에 노인정이 새로 생겼어요.
examples.en: A new senior center opened in the apartment complex.
On the holiday we took fruit to the senior center.
The grandmothers are chatting in front of the senior center.

explain: 마을이나 아파트 단지에 있어서 어르신들이 모여 쉬는 곳이에요. 공식적인 이름으로는 '경로당'도 많이 써요. 보통 '노인정에 가다/다니다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is a place inside a village or apartment complex where elders gather to relax. The official name '경로당' is also widely used. People say '노인정에 가다' or '노인정에 다니다'.

examples.ko: 노인층을 위한 일자리가 점점 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: Jobs for the elderly are gradually increasing.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 노인층에게 인기가 별로 없어요.
examples.en: This app isn't very popular among older people.

examples.ko: 우리나라는 노인층 인구 비율이 빠르게 높아지고 있어요.
examples.en: The proportion of elderly people in Korea is rising quickly.

examples.ko: 노인층의 건강을 위해 무료 검진을 해요.
examples.en: They offer free checkups for the health of the elderly.
Smartphone training is really necessary for older people.
This drama has many elderly viewers.

explain: '청년층', '중년층'처럼 나이대를 하나로 묶어 말할 때 써요. 한 사람에게는 쓰지 않고, 통계나 뉴스에서 집단을 말할 때 주로 써요. 한 사람을 높여 부를 때는 '어르신'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Like '청년층' and '중년층', it groups people by age bracket. It is not used for one individual but for a group, mostly in statistics and news. For one respected older person, say '어르신'.

examples.en: I bought fish-shaped pastries from a street vendor lady.
On my way home from work I bought fruit from a street stall.

examples.ko: 시장 앞 노점상들이 비가 오면 장사를 일찍 접어요.
examples.en: The street vendors in front of the market close early when it rains.

examples.ko: 노점상 할아버지가 덤으로 귤을 더 주셨어요.
examples.en: The old street vendor gave me extra tangerines for free.
I heard the district office has started cracking down on street vendors.
There are so many street vendors in Myeongdong.

explain: 길가에 자리를 잡고 물건을 파는 가게나 그 일을 하는 사람을 가리켜요. '포장마차'는 천막을 친 간이 가게를 말해서, 노점상 중 한 종류예요. 뉴스에서는 '노점상 단속'처럼 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to a roadside stall or the person who runs one. A '포장마차' is a tent-covered stall, so it is one kind of street vendor. News often uses it in phrases like '노점상 단속' (street vendor crackdown).

examples.ko: 날씨가 좋아서 노천카페에 앉아 커피를 마셨어요.
examples.en: The weather was nice, so I sat at an open-air cafe and had coffee.
A pretty open-air cafe opened by the river.
At an open-air cafe it's nice to watch people passing by.
When it rains, the open-air cafe closes.
We decided to have breakfast at an open-air cafe.

examples.ko: 유럽 여행 때 갔던 노천카페가 제일 기억에 남아요.
examples.en: The open-air cafe I visited on my Europe trip is what I remember most.

explain: 건물 밖 야외 자리에 의자와 탁자를 놓은 카페예요. 요즘 말로는 '야외 테라스'나 '테라스 카페'라고도 많이 해요. 날씨가 좋은 날 약속 장소로 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is a cafe with tables and chairs outdoors. These days people also say '테라스 카페' or '야외 테라스'. People often mention it as a meeting place on nice-weather days.

examples.en: I boiled mung beans into porridge and ate it.
I bought a bag of mung beans at the market.
My mother made mung bean pancakes for me.
They say mung bean porridge is good for the body in hot summer.
You have to soak the mung beans and grind them.
Bean sprouts are sprouted from mung beans.

explain: 한국 음식에서는 '녹두전'(빈대떡), '녹두죽'처럼 요리 이름에 많이 붙어요. 숙주나물도 녹두로 키우는 거라 같이 알아 두면 좋아요. 껍질을 벗긴 녹두는 노란색이에요.
explain_en: In Korean food it often forms dish names like '녹두전' (mung bean pancake) and '녹두죽'. Bean sprouts (숙주나물) are also grown from mung beans, so they are good to learn together. Hulled mung beans are yellow.

examples.en: You can get starch from potatoes.
If you add starch to the sauce, it thickens.

examples.ko: 녹말은 쌀, 감자, 옥수수에 많이 들어 있어요.
examples.en: Starch is found in large amounts in rice, potatoes and corn.
I coat the meat with starch and fry it.

examples.ko: 밥을 오래 씹으면 녹말이 달콤한 맛으로 바뀌어요.
examples.en: If you chew rice for a long time, the starch turns sweet.

examples.ko: 이 당면은 고구마 녹말로 만든 거예요.
examples.en: These glass noodles are made from sweet potato starch.

explain: 과학 시간이나 교과서에서는 '녹말'을 쓰고, 요리할 때는 '전분'이라는 말도 많이 써요. 감자, 고구마, 옥수수 같은 재료 이름 뒤에 붙여 '감자 녹말'처럼 말해요. 발음이 [농말]이라는 점에 주의하세요.
explain_en: Science classes and textbooks use '녹말', while cooking often uses '전분' too. You attach it to ingredients, as in '감자 녹말' (potato starch). Note that it is pronounced [농말].

examples.en: Dissolve the starch powder in water and add it.
I bought a bag of starch powder at the mart.
I make the batter for sweet and sour pork with starch powder.

examples.ko: 국이 너무 묽으면 녹말가루를 조금 넣어요.
examples.en: If the soup is too thin, I add a little starch powder.

examples.ko: 녹말가루가 다 떨어져서 다시 사야 해요.
examples.en: We ran out of starch powder, so we have to buy more.
First mix the starch powder into cold water.

explain: 요리법에서 많이 나오는 재료 이름이에요. 마트에서는 '전분'이나 '감자 전분'이라고 적혀 있기도 해요. 뜨거운 물보다 찬물에 먼저 풀어야 덩어리지지 않아요.
explain_en: It is a common ingredient name in recipes. At the mart the label may read '전분' or '감자 전분' instead. Dissolve it in cold water first so it doesn't clump.

examples.en: The building is old, so rusty water comes out of the tap.

examples.ko: 철제 난간에서 녹물이 흘러 벽이 얼룩졌어요.
examples.en: Rusty water ran from the iron railing and stained the wall.
After running it a while, the rusty water became clear.
Rusty water got into the laundry and the clothes turned yellowish.
Because of the rusty water, we decided to replace the water pipes.

examples.ko: 녹물이 묻은 곳은 바로 닦아 주세요.
examples.en: Please wipe the rust-stained spot right away.

explain: 쇠가 녹슬어 붉은 갈색을 띠는 물이에요. 쇠에 슨 '녹' 자체와 구분해서, '녹이 슬다', '녹물이 나오다/들다'처럼 짝지어 써요. 발음은 [농물]이에요.
explain_en: It is the reddish-brown water that comes from rusted iron. Distinguish it from '녹' (the rust itself): '녹이 슬다' (rust forms) and '녹물이 나오다/들다' (rusty water comes out/stains). It is pronounced [농물].

examples.en: The sugar dissolves into the warm water.

examples.ko: 새로 온 친구가 우리 반에 금방 녹아들었어요.
examples.en: The new friend blended into our class quickly.

examples.ko: 이 노래에는 우리 전통 소리가 자연스럽게 녹아들어 있어요.
examples.en: Our traditional sounds are naturally blended into this song.

examples.ko: 처음엔 어색했지만 이제 회사 분위기에 녹아들었어요.
examples.en: It was awkward at first, but now I've fit into the company atmosphere.

examples.ko: 작가의 마음이 이 그림에 녹아들어 있어요.
examples.en: The artist's feelings are infused into this painting.

examples.ko: 소금이 국물에 다 녹아들어서 보이지 않아요.
examples.en: The salt has completely dissolved into the broth and can't be seen.

explain: '~에 녹아들다' 모양으로 쓰고, 물질이 섞이는 경우와 사람이 집단에 어울리는 경우에 모두 써요. '스며들다'와 비슷하지만, 따로 구분이 안 될 만큼 하나가 되는 느낌이 강해요. '분위기에 녹아들다', '문화에 녹아들다'처럼 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is used as '~에 녹아들다' both for substances mixing and for people fitting into a group. It is close to '스며들다' but feels more like becoming one with it so nothing stands out. Common examples are '분위기에 녹아들다' and '문화에 녹아들다'.

en: cultivating a paddy field; rice farming

examples.ko: 이 지역은 논농사를 짓기 좋은 곳이에요.
examples.en: This area is a good place for rice farming.
My grandfather did only rice farming all his life.
Paddy farming needs a lot of water.

examples.ko: 우리 마을은 밭농사보다 논농사가 더 많아요.
examples.en: In our village there is more paddy farming than field farming.
These days paddy farming is mostly done by machine.
In spring we get busy preparing for rice farming.

explain: 짝이 되는 말은 '밭농사'예요. '논농사를 짓다'처럼 '짓다'와 같이 써요. 벼농사와 거의 같은 뜻으로 쓰이는 일이 많지만, '논'에서 하는 농사 전체를 말해요.
explain_en: Its counterpart is '밭농사' (dry-field farming). It pairs with the verb '짓다', as in '논농사를 짓다'. It is often close to '벼농사' (rice farming), but refers to all farming done in paddies.

examples.en: That remark became a controversy again.
This policy has many controversial points.

examples.ko: 저는 괜히 논란거리를 만들고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to create controversy for no reason.

examples.ko: 사진 한 장이 큰 논란거리로 번졌어요.
examples.en: A single photo grew into a big controversy.
That issue is already a long-standing controversy.

examples.ko: 새 규칙이 학교에서 논란거리가 되고 있어요.
examples.en: The new rule is becoming a point of debate at school.

explain: '논란이 되다'와 가깝지만, '논란거리'는 논란을 일으키는 문제나 일 자체를 가리켜요. '논란거리가 되다/없다/많다'처럼 말해요. 발음은 [놀란꺼리]예요.
explain_en: It is close to '논란이 되다', but '논란거리' points to the issue itself that causes controversy. Typical patterns are '논란거리가 되다/없다/많다'. It is pronounced [놀란꺼리].

examples.en: I took a logic class at university.
The logic professor gave us a hard problem.
Philosophy students always study logic.
The logic book was too hard, so I gave up.
My younger sibling says math is easier than logic.
I studied all night for the logic exam.

explain: '논리'는 생각이 이어지는 짜임이고, '논리학'은 그것을 공부하는 학문이에요. 철학, 수학과 가까워요. '논리적이다'와 헷갈리지 마세요. 발음은 [놀리학]이에요.
explain_en: '논리' is how thoughts connect, and '논리학' is the field that studies it, close to philosophy and math. Don't mix it up with '논리적이다' (logical). It is pronounced [놀리학].

examples.ko: 군청 앞 게시판에 농기계 임대 안내문이 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: A notice about renting farm machinery is posted on the board in front of the county office.
Thanks to farm machines, the work became much easier.
My father repairs the farm machines himself.
These days even rice planting is done with farm machines.
Farm machine accidents happen every year, which is worrying.
To borrow farm machinery, you have to submit an application.

explain: 트랙터, 콤바인처럼 동력으로 움직이는 기계를 말해요. 호미나 낫처럼 손으로 쓰는 도구는 '농기구'라고 해서 구분해요. '농기계를 빌리다/몰다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to powered machines such as tractors and combines. Hand tools like hoes and sickles are '농기구', which is the distinction. Typical verbs are '농기계를 빌리다/몰다'.

examples.en: The shed is full of old farming tools.
My grandfather keeps his farming tools wiped clean.
Hoes and sickles are typical farming tools.
I saw a shop selling farming tools at the market.

examples.ko: 농기구를 쓸 때는 다치지 않게 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful not to get hurt when you use farming tools.
I looked at old farming tools at the museum.

explain: 호미, 삽, 낫처럼 손으로 쓰는 도구가 먼저 떠오르는 말이에요. 트랙터 같은 동력 기계는 '농기계'라고 해요. 박물관이나 역사 이야기에서도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It first brings to mind hand tools like hoes, shovels and sickles. Powered machines like tractors are '농기계'. It also comes up often at museums and in history talk.

examples.en: It's the busy farming season, so the countryside is flat out with work.
During the busy farming season, we head to the field early in the morning.
When the busy season comes, there aren't enough hands.
We picked the wedding date to avoid the busy farming season.
College students took part in helping out during the busy farming season.
It's the busy season now, so it's hard to reach my parents by phone.

explain: 반대말은 일이 적은 때를 뜻하는 '농한기'예요. 일상에서는 '농사철'이 더 자연스럽고, '농번기'는 뉴스나 공지에서 많이 써요. '농번기 일손 돕기'처럼 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '농한기' (the slack farming season). In daily talk '농사철' sounds more natural, while '농번기' is common in news and announcements. A typical phrase is '농번기 일손 돕기'.

examples.ko: 이 농장은 친환경 농법으로 쌀을 키워요.
examples.en: This farm grows rice using eco-friendly farming methods.

examples.ko: 옛날 농법에는 조상의 지혜가 담겨 있어요.
examples.en: Old farming methods hold the wisdom of our ancestors.
Thanks to the new farming method, the harvest increased.
The taste of the fruit differs depending on the farming method.
I'm learning traditional farming methods from my grandfather.

examples.ko: 이 유기농 농법은 농약을 쓰지 않아요.
examples.en: This organic farming method does not use pesticides.

explain: 혼자 쓰기보다 '친환경 농법', '전통 농법', '유기농 농법'처럼 앞에 꾸미는 말과 함께 자주 써요. 발음은 [농뻡]이에요. 일상에서는 '농사 방법'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is used more often with a modifier, as in '친환경 농법', '전통 농법' and '유기농 농법'. It is pronounced [농뻡]. In casual talk people also say '농사 방법'.

examples.en: My father lived his whole life as a farmer.

examples.ko: 저 농사꾼 아저씨는 일 솜씨가 대단해요.
examples.en: That farmer uncle is really skilled at his work.
A farmer's hands are rough but warm.
I also want to become a farmer someday.
He is from Seoul but works like a farmer.
Farmers can't help being sensitive to the weather.

explain: 일상 대화에서 편하게 쓰는 말이에요. 격식 있는 자리나 글에서는 '농부'나 '농민'이 더 무난해요. '-꾼'은 어떤 일을 잘하거나 즐겨 하는 사람 뒤에 붙는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is a casual, everyday word. In formal settings or writing, '농부' or '농민' is safer. The suffix '-꾼' attaches to someone who does a particular job or does it habitually.

examples.ko: 품앗이는 농사철에 서로 일손을 빌려주던 상부상조의 방법이었어요.
examples.en: Pumasi was a way of mutual help where people lent each other labor in the farming season.

examples.ko: 농사철이 되면 시골은 눈코 뜰 새 없이 바빠요.
examples.en: When farming season comes, the countryside gets extremely busy.

examples.ko: 올해 농사철에는 비가 많이 와서 걱정이에요.
examples.en: It rained a lot this farming season, which is worrying.
Ahead of farming season, we check the farm machines.

examples.ko: 농사철에는 도시에서 일손을 도우러 오는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: In farming season, some people come from the city to help.
When farming season ends, the village holds a feast.

explain: '농번기'와 비슷하지만 일상 대화에서는 '농사철'이 더 자연스러워요. '농사철이 되다/시작되다/끝나다'처럼 시간의 흐름과 함께 써요. 일이 적은 때는 '농한기'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is similar to '농번기', but '농사철' sounds more natural in daily talk. It goes with time-flow verbs like '농사철이 되다/시작되다/끝나다'. The slack period is called '농한기'.

examples.ko: 이번 여름 방학에 농활을 가기로 했어요.
examples.en: I decided to go on a farm volunteer trip this summer vacation.
On the farm volunteer trip, I helped dig up garlic.
College students visited the village for farm volunteering.

examples.ko: 농활 때 마을 어르신들과 정이 많이 들었어요.
examples.en: During the farm volunteer trip I grew close to the village elders.

examples.ko: 처음 간 농활이 너무 힘들었지만 보람 있었어요.
examples.en: My first farm volunteer trip was very hard but rewarding.
Our club is taking applications for the farm volunteer trip.

explain: '농촌 봉사 활동'의 줄임말로, 대학생 동아리나 학과에서 단체로 가는 경우가 많아요. '농활을 가다/다녀오다'처럼 말해요. 일상 대화에서도 그대로 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is a shortened form of '농촌 봉사 활동' (rural volunteer activity), and university clubs or departments often go as a group. Say '농활을 가다/다녀오다'. It is used as-is in everyday conversation.

examples.en: The wall is quite high, so I can't see inside.
The kite is floating high up in the sky.
There is a bird's nest at the top of a tall tree.
The ceiling is high, so sounds echo.
It isn't very high, but it is a sturdy fence.
Books are piled up high.

explain: '높다'보다 눈에 꽤 높게 보인다는 느낌이 있어서, 담, 천장, 쌓인 물건처럼 눈으로 보이는 것에 잘 써요. ㅎ 불규칙이라서 '높다래요', '높다란'으로 바뀌어요. 말할 때는 그냥 '높다'를 훨씬 많이 써요.
explain_en: It carries a feel of looking quite high to the eye, so it suits things you can see, like walls, ceilings or stacked items. It is an ㅎ-irregular, so it becomes '높다래요' and '높다란'. In speech, plain '높다' is far more common.

examples.ko: 피아노 오른손 악보에는 보통 높은음자리표가 나와요.
examples.en: Right-hand piano parts usually have a treble clef.
I learned how to draw a treble clef.
Violin sheet music has a treble clef.
I can see the treble clef at the very beginning of the score.
It is hard to tell the treble clef and the bass clef apart.
My younger sibling drew a treble clef nicely.

explain: 음악 시간에 배우는 말이고, 반대는 '낮은음자리표'예요. 띄어 쓰지 않고 한 단어로 붙여 써요. 피아노 오른손 악보, 바이올린, 플루트 악보에 주로 나와요.
explain_en: You learn it in music class, and its opposite is '낮은음자리표' (bass clef). It is written as one word without spaces. It mainly appears in right-hand piano parts and in violin and flute scores.

examples.en: I let the fish I caught go again.
I set the bird free to fly away.
Please, let that person go now.
When I let the cat go, it ran away immediately.

examples.ko: 아이 손을 놔주면 길을 잃을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you let go of the child's hand, they could get lost.
I still haven't been able to let go of my old lover.

explain: '놓아주다'의 줄임말이라서 말할 때 훨씬 많이 써요. '놔줘요', '놔줬어요'로 활용해요. 마음에서 사람이나 감정을 보내 주는 비유로도 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is the contracted form of '놓아주다' and is used much more in speech. It conjugates as '놔줘요' and '놔줬어요'. It is also often used figuratively for letting a person or feeling go emotionally.

examples.ko: 뇌세포는 한번 죽으면 다시 살아나기 어렵대요.
examples.en: They say brain cells are hard to bring back once they die.
We looked at a picture of brain cells in science class.
Brain cells were damaged in the accident.

examples.ko: 새로운 걸 배우면 뇌세포가 자극을 받아요.
examples.en: Learning something new stimulates your brain cells.
Each brain cell sends and receives signals from the others.

examples.ko: 머리를 너무 썼더니 뇌세포가 다 죽은 것 같아요.
examples.en: I used my head so much that it feels like all my brain cells died.

explain: 과학 이야기에도 쓰지만, 일상에서는 우스갯소리로 '뇌세포가 죽다'라고 많이 말해요. 어이없는 일이나 너무 힘든 공부를 했을 때 쓰는 농담이에요. 비슷한 말로 '신경세포'가 있어요.
explain_en: It is used in science, but in daily life people joke '뇌세포가 죽다' (my brain cells died) after something absurd or exhausting studying. A related term is '신경세포' (nerve cell).

examples.en: Who all is coming to tonight's gathering?
Who all are you going to invite to the party?
Please tell me who the class president candidates are.
Who all decided to go on this trip?
I'm curious who passed the exam.
Who all did you tell this news to?

explain: '누구'와 달리 여러 사람이 있을 거라고 생각하고 물을 때 써요. 이름을 정확히 말하고 싶지 않을 때 '누구누구 씨가 그랬대'처럼 아무개 대신 둘러 말하기도 해요. 뒤에 '가', '한테', '이다' 같은 조사가 그대로 붙어요.
explain_en: Unlike '누구', you use it when you expect several people in the answer. It can also stand in for names you don't want to say, as in '누구누구 씨가 그랬대' (so-and-so said that). Particles like '가', '한테' and '이다' attach as usual.

examples.en: The pages of the old book have all turned yellow.
When autumn comes, the rice plants turn yellow.
The white T-shirt turned yellowish from sweat.

examples.ko: 햇빛을 오래 받으면 책 표지가 누레질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If exposed to sunlight for long, a book cover can turn yellow.
The wallpaper is old and turning yellow.

examples.ko: 이가 누레지지 않게 양치를 잘해야 해요.
examples.en: You should brush well so your teeth don't turn yellow.

explain: '누렇다'에서 나온 말이고 ㅎ 불규칙이라 '누레져요', '누레졌어요'로 써요. 작고 가벼운 느낌의 말은 '노래지다'예요. 색이 변하는 과정을 말하는 동사라서, 이미 누런 상태는 '누렇다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It comes from '누렇다' and is an ㅎ-irregular, so it becomes '누레져요' and '누레졌어요'. The lighter, smaller-feeling version is '노래지다'. It describes the process of changing color, while the state of already being yellow is '누렇다'.

examples.ko: 누리꾼들이 이 영상에 댓글을 많이 달았어요.
examples.en: Netizens left lots of comments on this video.

examples.ko: 한 누리꾼이 올린 사진이 화제가 됐어요.
examples.en: A photo posted by one netizen became a hot topic.
This song is popular among netizens.
Netizens were greatly surprised after seeing the news.
The netizens' reaction was incredibly fast.
Online, netizens share information with one another.

explain: '네티즌'을 우리말로 바꾼 말이에요. 뉴스 기사에서는 '누리꾼'을 많이 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '네티즌'도 자주 써요. 온라인 댓글이나 반응을 전할 때 나오는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is the native Korean replacement for 'netizen' ('네티즌'). News articles often use '누리꾼', while everyday talk also uses '네티즌'. It shows up when reporting online comments or reactions.
